cortes_plano.ideia: Kenji abre o armário e é soterrado por tudo o que já começou e largou: violão, halteres, tênis, um caderno com um desenho só. Toda coisa nova é mágica… até o terceiro dia. Aí o Oni sussurra uma novidade, e ele diz sim de novo.

cortes_plano.gancho: ONI: this one is the one.
cortes_plano.ideia: O Oni da preguiça traz uma caixa brilhante atrás da outra, e a pilha de hobbies largados cresce junto com ele. Um ano inteiro de primeiros dias: vinte começos, nenhum fim — até a única faca da casa perder o fio.
Numa lojinha da rua, um velho afiador usa a mesma pedra há cinquenta anos. Kenji escolhe uma coisa só — o mesmo omelete enrolado, todo dia —, fecha cada caixa nova do Oni e, no centésimo, acerta.

titulos: His Hand Moved Before He Did. | An Animated Short Film
Can't Stop Scrolling at Night? | An Animated Short Film
videos.descricao:
Phone addiction at night: why your hand grabs the phone before you even decide, and what one pause can change.

By day, Kenji is fine. He works. He smiles. But at 2:00 AM the phone lights up, and his thumb does the rest.
Something climbs out of the screen. Night after night, the Oni gets bigger and Kenji gets smaller.
Then, one sleepless night, a sound comes from the old man's garden next door: drip, drip, clack.

MA (間): the pause, the space between. In Japanese, ma is the interval of space and time between two things; in the arts (Noh, music) it is the empty beat between one sound and the next. The film uses the word as an image, not as a medical method.

Sources: Kotobank, 間 (Daijisen, Nihon Kokugo Daijiten) · Jisho, 間 (ま): "time; pause; space" · Kotobank, 鹿威し (shishi-odoshi, the bamboo water pipe of Japanese gardens).

titulos: When Motivation Never Comes: The Japanese Word Ikigai
He Waited 120 Days for the Spark. It Never Came.
videos.descricao:
What do you do when motivation never comes? This animated short film answers with one Japanese word: ikigai.

Every night, Kenji lights a candle by the window and waits for the spark. At night he makes big plans: run, learn, build something, be someone. Every morning at 7:00 the flame is gone, and the Oni of laziness pulls the blanket back up.
Day 9. Day 30. Day 70. The candles get bigger, the flames get shorter.
Then, one rainy morning at 6:00, there is a small sound at the door.

IKIGAI (生き甲斐): a reason for living, what makes life worth living. In everyday Japanese it is not a grand life plan, just the reason you get up in the morning.
Find a reason. Not a spark.

Meaning of the word: Daijisen dictionary (kotobank.jp/word/生き甲斐) · "Ikigai", Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ikigai).

Bowl 20. Still Empty. | An Animated Short Film
videos.titulo_escolhido: HARA HACHI BU | An Animated Short Film
videos.descricao:
Hara Hachi Bu: why do you never feel satisfied, even when you have everything? An old Japanese saying has a quiet answer.

Kenji never stops at enough. His ramen bowl fills itself back up, every episode rolls into the next, and the game runs until sunrise. He is always full, but nothing tastes like anything anymore.
And someone keeps the bowl full: a smiling Oni with a ladle.
Then one evening a neighbor's grocery bag breaks, and Kenji stays for dinner.

HARA HACHI BU (腹八分, "eight parts of ten") is an old Japanese saying about eating: stop when your stomach is about eight parts of ten full, before you are stuffed. In this film it becomes a way to look at everything we binge.
"Leave room. Joy lives there."

Sources for the saying: Daijisen dictionary on Kotobank (kotobank.jp/word/腹八分) · Jisho (jisho.org/search/腹八分).
